name: Uptone AI
tagline: An AI assistant that rewrites your messages and emails to sound clearer, warmer, or more professional before you hit send.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Tone rewriting is the single most commoditized thing a language model does: you send text plus an instruction, you get text back. There is no dataset here you cannot approximate with a decent system prompt and three or four named presets. The only genuinely hard part is the delivery mechanism, a global hotkey that grabs your selection, rewrites it, and pastes it back without you leaving the app you are in, and that is a known, solved pattern in Electron or Tauri. You will pay an API bill instead of a subscription, and for a normal volume of emails that bill is small. What you do not get is someone else tuning the prompts until the output stops sounding like a press release.
coreLoopDIY: A menubar app with a global hotkey that takes your selected text, rewrites it in a chosen tone via an LLM API, and pastes the result back in place.
requirements: An LLM API key, or a local model served over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Accessibility or input-monitoring permission on macOS for the global hotkey and paste
whatYouLose: Prompt tuning that someone else already iterated on, your first drafts of the presets will sound stiff
A mobile keyboard, so phone email stays untouched
Deep per-app integration with Gmail, Outlook, Slack and the like; clipboard interception is blunter
Account sync, so your presets and history live on one machine
Someone to blame and email when the rewrite mangles a sentence
moatNotes: The moat is prompt taste and the fiddly OS plumbing, not the model. Both are copyable, one just takes longer than you think.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the thin wrapper is thin only after someone has spent months finding out which instructions make a model stop adding 'I hope this email finds you well.' Paying also means no API key management, no permission dialogs, and something that works the same on your laptop and your phone. If you write client-facing messages all day, that consistency is worth more than the subscription. If you rewrite four emails a week, it very much is not.
notes: The interesting engineering here is the global hotkey and the paste-back, not the AI part.
prompt:
Build a local macOS-first menubar app called Tone that rewrites selected text in place.

Stack, no substitutions: Electron with TypeScript, electron-builder for packaging, no framework for the small settings UI, just plain HTML and CSS.

Core loop:
1. Register a global shortcut, Cmd+Shift+U by default.
2. On trigger, copy the current selection by sending a synthetic Cmd+C, read the clipboard, and remember the previous clipboard contents.
3. Send the text to an OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint with a system prompt for the currently selected tone.
4. Write the rewritten text to the clipboard and send a synthetic Cmd+V to replace the selection.
5. Restore the original clipboard after a short delay.

Tones: ship exactly five presets, Professional, Warm, Direct, Apologetic, Shorter. Each is a separate system prompt stored in a JSON file the user can edit. Rules baked into every prompt: preserve meaning and facts, keep the original language, never add greetings or sign-offs that were not there, return only the rewritten text with no preamble.

Menubar menu: pick active tone, open settings, quit. Settings window lets the user set the model name, the base URL, and the hotkey, persisted to a local JSON config in app userData.

Also include a small always-on-top preview window mode, toggleable in settings: instead of pasting directly, show the rewrite with Accept and Discard buttons.

Secrets: read OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_BASE_URL from a .env file in dev, and from the settings config in the packaged app. Ship a .env.example. Never log the text or the key.

Out of scope, do not build: accounts, cloud sync, telemetry, analytics, usage dashboards, a mobile app, browser extensions, per-app integrations.

Handle the failure cases honestly: empty selection, missing API key, network error, and missing accessibility permission each show a native notification explaining what to do.

Deliver a README with build steps, the macOS permissions the app needs and why, and a one-line note on the roughly known cost per rewrite.
